reviews.reasons: A conditional outreach test is a reasonable shape, but the plan's live test decides only CURRENT_DEMAND and CONVERSION while four other links it relies on are unestablished and are not things only a live sale can measure. FULFILMENT and ECONOMICS rest on RECOMMENDATION facts only (a $250 Fiverr gig page, a $400 build ESTIMATE, no quote for the actual scope - 5 pages plus booking integration plus written eye-care copy, which a $250 template gig does not include); Brain marks both not established. These can be settled by research/quote at $0 before any practice is asked to pay $2,500 up front, yet no step obtains a quote before the sale - the 'quote above $500: stop' rule fires only after money has been taken (day 10), which would force a refund. OFFER_AND_PRICE is measured by the same test (a paid order at $2,500) and should be listed in validation.decides; the only published price evidence (agency bands) was rejected at the evidence gate as a seller's price list. The test's proof (one paid order by day 10) also does not decide the target of two deals: at ~1/150 it implies ~300 contacts for the second, with no rule for when deal 2 must close to deliver and settle by day 30.
findings: Recomputed: 2 x $2,500 = $5,000 collected; direct cost 2 x $400 = $800 (ESTIMATE); max exposure $400 (owner advance day 10) <= $500 cap; Stripe 2.9% + 30c leaves ~$4,854 paid out - fine under COLLECTED_CASH but not if 'make $5,000' is read as net.
Delivery promise inconsistent with the schedule: offer says 10-day delivery, but deal 1 (paid day 8) is delivered day 20 and deal 2 (paid day 14) day 27.

Add a step 0: get a written quote from a named developer for the exact scope (pages, booking link, copy) before outreach; then FULFILMENT/ECONOMICS rest on evidence and the stop rule protects buyers' money.

Size the test to the target: proof should state what day-10 result makes two paid deals by ~day 17-20 credible (e.g. contact count/close-rate threshold), with a continue rule for further outreach and a stop if deal 2 is not paid by a stated day.

The 1,200 NPI-2 records are a superset (includes ophthalmology/multi-specialty and chains); enough for 150 contacts, but 'EVIDENCED' should be a lower bound on organisations, not on independent practices.
SETTLES_IN_TIME: first Stripe payout up to 14 days for some industries; deal 2 paid day 14 settles by day 28 at worst - inside 30, but with no slack.

conditions.why: The card's fulfillment fact is a RECOMMENDATION (a Fiverr gig tier range); no EVIDENCE fact names a developer who has quoted or agreed to build this scope (5 pages, booking link, eye-care copy) in time.
directCosts $400 is a RECOMMENDATION/ESTIMATE; no quote establishes the build cost for the scope, so margin and the $500 exposure fit are not evidenced.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now a startable, bounded plan. The unknowns it rests on - whether an independent practice buys from a cold approach at $2,500, and at what close rate - are ones only a live offer measures, and the plan names them in validation.decides together with price. FULFILMENT and ECONOMICS are settled before any buyer is contacted (step q0: a named developer's written quote <= $500 for the exact scope, stop otherwise), so no practice's money is taken without a fulfiller. Recomputed: 2 x $2,500 = $5,000 collected (COLLECTED_CASH, so gross meets the metric); builds 2 x $400 + Stripe fees 2 x $72.80 = $945.60; net $4,054.40; max exposure $400 (owner advance day 10) <= $500 cap, deal 2's build paid from deal 1's settled payout; proof day 10; deal 2 stop at day 16. Proof/stop/continue are sized to the two-deal target and every prior finding and both conditions are answered.
findings: Worst-case timing: if the first Stripe payout takes the full 14 days, deal 1 settles day 22 and deal 2's build is ordered day 22; a <=10-day build then lands as late as day 32, after the window and past the 'within 14 days of payment' promise for a deal paid day 14-16. The q0 quote should require <= 6-day delivery (the referenced Fiverr gig advertises 2 days) or the stop should fire earlier.
Owner hours total ~16.5 h plus writing the eye-care copy from Brain drafts (not counted); the goal sets no hours limit, so this fits, but the copy hours should be measured on deal 1.
The NPI count is correctly relabelled as a lower bound on optometrist-taxonomy organisation records, a superset of independent practices; 300 contacts out of 1,200+ is plausible.
The agency price band (s2) is correctly labelled as a seller's price list, not observed payments; the plan does not lean on it as the price.

sources.claim: Offer price $2,500 (a hypothesis recorded on the card)
Optometrist website design cost lands between $2,000 and $25,000 depending on scope (agency-published price list, not observed payments)
At least 1,200 optometrist organization records in Ohio, each with address and phone: the buyers exist and can be reached
Fiverr gig: 5-page WordPress business website within 2 days for $250 — a fulfiller of this kind exists
First Stripe payout typically 7 days, up to 14 for some industries
Private practice share of the optometric workforce fell from 51% to 41% (2017-2024)

validation.proof: Day 1: a named developer's written quote <= $500 for the exact scope with <= 10-day delivery. Day 10: at least one practice has signed and paid $2,500 from the first 150 contacts and at least 3 more qualified replies are open, so a second paid deal by day 16 is credible
stop: No developer quote <= $500 for the scope on day 1-2: stop before contacting any practice
No paid order by day 10 after 150 personalised contacts: stop, spend nothing on builds
Deal 2 not paid by day 16: stop selling (no time to build and settle by day 30); deliver deal 1 only
Two or more replies objecting to the price: re-offer once at $2,000 and re-measure on the next 100 contacts
continue: Quote obtained: start outreach on day 2
One paid order and >= 3 qualified replies by day 10: order deal 1, contact 150 more practices on days 10-12 to close deal 2 by day 16

answers.finding: Recomputed: $5,000 collected; Stripe fee leaves ~$4,854 paid out
answers.resolution: Accepted: Stripe fees now appear as FEE outflows on the collect step; the contract metric is COLLECTED_CASH, so gross collections of $5,000 meet it.

answers.finding: Delivery promise inconsistent with the schedule
answers.resolution: Accepted: the offer now promises delivery within 14 days of payment, which both deals meet (deal 1 paid day 8, delivered day 20; deal 2 paid day 14, delivered day 27).

answers.finding: Add a step 0: written quote from a named developer for the exact scope before outreach
answers.resolution: Accepted: step q0 obtains the quote on day 1 and the plan stops before any practice is contacted if no quote <= $500 exists, so no buyer money is ever taken without a fulfiller.

answers.finding: Size the test to the target
answers.resolution: Accepted: proof now requires one paid order plus >= 3 open qualified replies by day 10, a continue rule of 150 more contacts on days 10-12, and a stop if deal 2 is not paid by day 16.

answers.finding: The 1,200 NPI-2 records are a superset
answers.resolution: Accepted: the quantity is renamed as a lower bound on optometrist-taxonomy organization records, not on independent practices.

answers.finding: SETTLES_IN_TIME: first Stripe payout up to 14 days
answers.resolution: Accepted: deal 2's build is ordered only once deal 1's payout has settled (day 22 at worst), using the quoted <= 10-day delivery; payment for deal 2 taken by day 16 settles by day 30 at worst (2-day rolling after the first payout).

answers.finding: FULFILMENT condition
answers.resolution: The card's fulfillment fact is a RECOMMENDATION; FULFILMENT is now measured by step q0's written quote before outreach and is in validation.decides.

review.reasons: CONDITIONAL is now a startable, bounded plan. The unknowns it rests on - whether an independent practice buys from a cold approach at $2,500, and at what close rate - are ones only a live offer measures, and the plan names them in validation.decides together with price. FULFILMENT and ECONOMICS are settled before any buyer is contacted (step q0: a named developer's written quote <= $500 for the exact scope, stop otherwise), so no practice's money is taken without a fulfiller. Recomputed: 2 x $2,500 = $5,000 collected (COLLECTED_CASH, so gross meets the metric); builds 2 x $400 + Stripe fees 2 x $72.80 = $945.60; net $4,054.40; max exposure $400 (owner advance day 10) <= $500 cap, deal 2's build paid from deal 1's settled payout; proof day 10; deal 2 stop at day 16. Proof/stop/continue are sized to the two-deal target and every prior finding and both conditions are answered.
findings: Worst-case timing: if the first Stripe payout takes the full 14 days, deal 1 settles day 22 and deal 2's build is ordered day 22; a <=10-day build then lands as late as day 32, after the window and past the 'within 14 days of payment' promise for a deal paid day 14-16. The q0 quote should require <= 6-day delivery (the referenced Fiverr gig advertises 2 days) or the stop should fire earlier.
Owner hours total ~16.5 h plus writing the eye-care copy from Brain drafts (not counted); the goal sets no hours limit, so this fits, but the copy hours should be measured on deal 1.
The NPI count is correctly relabelled as a lower bound on optometrist-taxonomy organisation records, a superset of independent practices; 300 contacts out of 1,200+ is plausible.
The agency price band (s2) is correctly labelled as a seller's price list, not observed payments; the plan does not lean on it as the price.

basis.intent: Make $5,000 in the next 30 days selling to independent optometry practices. I can spend up to $500 to get it going.
